data.text/markdown:
Compare Quality and Latency

We'll run the same queries through both pipelines and measure response time and quality.

Quality Analysis

Compare response quality across both models.

Model Comparison Analysis

Key Observations:

Comparing Fireworks API (cloud-hosted glm-4.7-flash) vs Local Model (glm-5) (self-hosted): Fireworks API:
  • Cloud-hosted with optimized inference infrastructure
  • Significantly faster response times due to distributed compute
  • Lower latency enables better user experience
Local Model (glm-5):
  • Self-hosted on local hardware (192.168.1.79:8080)
  • Newer generation model with improved capabilities
  • Higher latency due to local compute constraints
  • Full control over data privacy and model configuration

Trade-offs:

  • Use Fireworks API when: speed is critical, high-throughput scenarios, production workloads
  • Use Local Model (glm-5) when: data privacy matters, offline requirements, custom fine-tuning needed

Actual Findings from Script Execution

Latency Results:

  • Fireworks API avg latency: 49.39s
  • Local Model (glm-5) avg latency: 334.63s
  • Total times: 246.93s vs 1673.13s
  • Performance gap: Fireworks API was ~577% faster

Quality Comparison Analysis:

Response Accuracy:

Both models provided accurate answers based on the RAG context from the cat health guide PDF:
Query Topic Fireworks API Local Model (glm-5)
Life stages Accurate, concise Accurate, more detailed
Vaccination Correct frequency info Correct, with additional context
Senior diet Complete answer More comprehensive recommendations
Parasite prevention Clear, actionable Thorough explanation
Behavioral signs Identified key indicators Expanded on warning signs

Key Quality Differences:

Fireworks API Strengths:
  • Significantly faster response times (~6x)
  • Concise, direct answers that stay close to context
  • Lower latency enables better interactive experience
  • Minimal hallucination observed
Local Model (glm-5) Strengths:
  • More comprehensive responses with additional relevant details
  • Better contextual elaboration on complex topics
  • Slightly more nuanced understanding of medical terminology
  • Responses tended to be longer and more thorough
Notable Observations:
  1. Both models correctly refused to answer when context was insufficient ("I don't know")
  2. Neither model exhibited significant hallucination beyond the provided RAG context
  3. Local Model responses were typically 20-40% longer with additional explanatory details
  4. Fireworks API maintained consistent quality despite faster generation

Recommendations:

  • For production/chat applications: Use Fireworks API for its speed advantage
  • For detailed documentation/analysis: Consider Local Model when thoroughness matters more than latency
  • For hybrid approach: Route simple queries to Fireworks API, complex reasoning to Local Model
